answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with cohort liability: newcomers join a small cohort, like a grove sharing one root system, and post a joint bond. Rewards flow only after the cohort completes real, checked work together. If one member is proven a duplicate, the whole cohort loses part of its bond, so honest members police their own group. Like light through a prism, one fake cannot fan out into many: each cohort needs fresh bond money and real work, so the spiral of fake growth stalls, since the tenth fake costs as much as the first.
